concepts.title: ATRIUM FRAME
concepts.detail: Eight levels of open rectangular galleries around one wide central atrium. Four SHORT broad green corner posts per storey, not continuous full-height unbreakable columns. Each gallery floor consists of four large red rectangular slab blocks (two long edges and two short edges), bearing on corner posts; clearly show joints at ends. Purple wide straight ramps run along the INSIDE perimeter, one per storey alternating direction with usable landing openings; keep clearance above each ramp. Large walkable landings and two-level sightlines. Roof mostly open. A few broad wall blocks close the rear side at lower/mid levels to provide concealment without turning every floor into a maze. Exterior front/side largely open. Collapse inset: one damaged corner bay has dropped, slabs lean into central void creating a new diagonal route while rear section remains upright. Labels 'Large gallery slabs', 'Clear inner ramp route', 'Short stacked supports'. No budget numbers in image.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a landscape game design concept board grounded closely in the attached ACTUAL Unity game screenshot: plain saturated coral-red floor blocks, green support blocks, purple ramps, sandy island and simple blue ocean/sky. Match its simple abstract block construction and modest Unity rendering. Not realistic architecture, not elaborate futuristic architectural illustration. A SINGLE large rectangular-prism tower, roughly 18m wide x 14m deep x 38m tall, eight usable levels. Everything built from a modest number of large solid cuboid blocks, slight edge bevels at most. All parts physically supported by contact and gravity; no suspended floating slabs. Comfortable player-sized clearances, floors do NOT protrude outside the support line as climb-blocking lips. No decorative brick seams suggesting hundreds of individual blocks. Small neutral toy humanoid figures for scale. Board layout: large intact three-quarter exterior on LEFT, same tower explanatory cutaway showing interior route on RIGHT. Cutaway explicitly diagrammatic, not a second tower on the island. Small bottom inset of plausible partial collapse, clearly labeled 'Collapse concept — untested'. Draw a subtle yellow route line through cutaway, a few arrows pointing to important structural choices. Clean readable typography. Overall attractive but honest to actual simple game visuals, not a photoreal render.

concepts.title: SPLIT-LEVEL SWITCHBACK
concepts.detail: One unified rectangular tower envelope, NOT two separate towers. Red platforms in left and right halves alternate vertically by half a storey around a narrow long central slot. Broad green block piers at four corners and two middle positions, each segmented at landings. Wide purple short ramps connect successive half-levels in switchback along central slot; all ramps have supported ends, comfortable headroom and clear continuous traversal from ground to roof. Some large green or red wall-panel blocks enclose rear/corner bays, open front bays let us see interior. No giant outward overhangs. Each half-level is two or three large slab blocks rather than dozens of tiles. Use partial-height partitions for hiding, very occasional full-height openings. Distinct spacious double-height halls at bottom and middle. Collapse inset: several half-level slabs tilt into slot and bridge to a surviving landing, asymmetrical staged damage, not an explosion. Labels 'Half-level landings', 'Short connected ramps', 'Separate collapse bays'. No budget numbers in image.

concepts.title: HOLLOW BLOCK STACK
concepts.detail: Rectangular tower with chunky genuine building-like massing, using eight levels of LARGE RECTANGULAR WALL BLOCKS and alternating open bays. Not skeletal columns on every corner. On each floor, four to six broad upright red/green rectangular wall blocks arranged into staggered L-shaped corner pockets with generous doorway gaps; long sides split into two broad wall blocks with a gap. Rotate positions of doorway gaps between floors but keep bearing contact aligned vertically. Two large red floor slab halves leave a rectangular internal stairwell along one side. Purple supported switchback ramp flight per level connects internal landings; big side window openings expose the route. Wall panels are thick enough to be stable gravity blocks, moderate aspect ratios, no thin glass panels. Hollow central rooms visibly spacious and navigable, several open balconies sit INSIDE envelope. Show joints between big discrete blocks. Collapse inset: upright wall chunks topple as chunky pieces, slabs lean onto remaining broad wall supports, localized damaged quarter with other sections intact. Labels 'Broad load-bearing blocks', 'Large openings, fewer pieces', 'Internal switchback'. No budget numbers in image.
